title: Lost Teen Found Safe After Six Days in the Woods
summary:
A teenager lost in the Australian woods for six days is safe at home now.

William, 17, was found alive on Thursday next to a creek near Walhalla, a small town about 185 kilometres east of Melbourne. He had gone camping with a friend last Friday and got lost walking back for more gear.

A police helicopter crew saw him asleep on a flat rock by the creek. He woke up, gave a thumbs up, and was lifted up to safety. He wore no shirt and was sunburned, using towels as blankets.

Police said he was in good spirits and mostly in good health. He was taken to a hospital so doctors could keep an eye on him. His mother, Elizabeth, was overjoyed and joked that he was grounded for life.

William has Level 2 autism, which means he needs a lot of support. He walked for days over very steep ground and spent his last two days at the creek, about 2 kilometres from his campsite. More than 100 emergency workers and volunteers had joined the search.
why_it_matters: Learning what to do if you get lost outdoors, like staying in one place and staying warm, can help keep you safe.

keywords.explanation: A helicopter is an aircraft with spinning blades on top that can fly up, down, and hover in one place.
A creek is a small stream of water that flows through the land.
Sunburned means your skin is red and sore from spending too long in strong sun.
Autism is a way a person's brain works differently, which can mean they need extra help in daily life.
Volunteers are people who choose to help without being paid to do it.
